title: Model Hotel gateway
description: Model Hotel fleet: traffic, latency, tokens and spend, reliability and process from every member's /metrics.

panels.title: Up
panels.description: Share of scrape targets answering. 100% is every member up; anything less means a member is down or unreachable and the fleet totals below are missing its share.

panels.title: Requests/s
panels.description: Proxied requests per second across the selected providers.

panels.title: Error share
panels.description: Share of requests ending 4xx or 5xx. Client disconnects (499) are counted separately and excluded. Orange above 5%, red above 20%.

panels.title: p95 latency
panels.description: 95th percentile end-to-end request duration: 19 of 20 requests finish faster than this.

panels.title: p95 TTFT
panels.description: 95th percentile time to first token, streaming requests only. This is what a user feels as “it started answering”.

panels.title: Tokens/s
panels.description: Prompt plus completion tokens per second across the selected providers. reasoning and prompt_cached are subsets of those two kinds and are not added again.

Priced spend over the selected range, summed from modelhotel_cost_usd_total across members (an instant query at the range end, so 6h and 24h are computed at the same moment). Subscription providers are priced at their catalogue list price, so this is what the traffic would have cost, not what was billed. Approximate at the range edges and across member restarts, where the counter resets; a model with no known price adds nothing.
panels.title: Spend
Breakers
panels.description: Selected providers with a breaker not closed on any member. Zero is the healthy state; red means at least one of them is being routed around somewhere in the fleet. Providers the request path has not named yet (a seeded quota pin) share one unknown entry; series scraped before the gauge carried a provider name are left out.

targets.expr: count(max by (provider) (modelhotel_circuit_breaker_state{provider!="", provider=~"$provider"}) > 0) or on() vector(0)

panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: Time since the most recently restarted member came up (the youngest process in the fleet). A small number after nothing was deployed is a crash.

panels.title: Requests/s by status class
panels.description: Requests per second by status class, one line per class in a fixed colour: 2xx green, 3xx blue, 4xx yellow, 499 grey (the client went away), 5xx red, unknown purple. Not stacked, so the colour on top is the class that dominates. A series sits out while it is zero, so a class that has not happened in the range does not draw a flat line; the legend shows its peak, not a last value that would outlive the burst.

panels.title: Requests/s by provider
panels.description: Request rate stacked by upstream provider: who is actually carrying the traffic.

panels.title: Errors/s by kind
panels.description: Failed requests per second by the gateway's own classification (validation, provider_error, timeout, ...), not by HTTP status. Stacked: the total height is the error rate, each band one kind. A series sits out while it is zero, so a kind that has not happened in the range does not draw a flat line; the legend shows its peak, not a last value that would outlive the burst.

panels.title: Requests by model
panels.description: Top 20 provider / model / status combinations by request count over the dashboard time range. “model” is the name the CLIENT asked for; hotel/<group> means the request went through a failover group.

panels.title: Duration quantiles
panels.description: End-to-end request duration for the selected providers. A mean far below p95 means a slow tail, not a slow gateway.

panels.title: p95 duration by provider
panels.description: 95th percentile request duration per provider: which upstream is the slow one.

panels.title: TTFT quantiles
panels.description: Time to first token, streaming requests only. Gaps mean no streaming traffic in that window, not zero latency.

panels.title: p95 TTFT by provider
panels.description: 95th percentile time to first token per provider: which upstream is slow to start answering.

panels.title: Prompt cache hit share
panels.description: Share of prompt tokens the providers served from their prompt cache over the dashboard time range (kind prompt_cached over kind prompt). Cached input is billed at a fraction of the fresh rate, so this is the difference between the token volume and the bill.

panels.title: Tokens/s by kind
panels.description: Tokens per second by kind. reasoning is the share of completion the provider reported as thinking, not a third bucket, so the lines are not stacked: prompt and completion are the whole throughput, reasoning sits inside completion, and prompt_cached is the share of prompt the provider served from its cache. Logarithmic Y axis: prompt tokens run one to three orders of magnitude above completion and reasoning tokens, which would otherwise draw as flat lines.

panels.title: Tokens by model
panels.description: Top 20 provider / model / kind combinations by tokens over the dashboard time range.

panels.title: Spend/h by provider
panels.description: Current burn rate in dollars per hour, stacked by provider: the token rate priced with the gateway's price table.

panels.title: Spend by model
panels.description: Top 20 provider / model pairs by dollars billed over the dashboard time range. Models that added nothing over the range (unpriced, or idle) are left out.

panels.title: Breaker state by provider
panels.description: Circuit-breaker state per enabled provider, the worst state any member reports for it: closed (green) is serving, half-open (orange) is probing after a cooldown, open (red) is refused traffic until the cooldown or quota pin ends. A provider nothing has routed to yet reads closed, since it is served as one; a blank stretch is a provider that was disabled or did not exist then. A lane that stays open across a scrape interval is a provider the fleet is routing around.

panels.title: Failover attempts/s
panels.description: Attempts beyond the first try, labelled with the provider the attempt went to (hedged launches included): the fan-out to fallback entries per provider.

panels.title: Responses API reroutes/s
panels.description: Requests re-sent on the other OpenAI dialect. learned = healed after a live 400; preemptive = the cache already knew.

panels.title: Retirement probes
panels.description: Probes that check whether a model still exists upstream, over the dashboard time range. refused = the provider refused the model by name (a retirement was attempted, not necessarily completed); served = called off; inconclusive = postponed.

panels.title: Upstream 429s/s by class
panels.description: Rate limits the upstream returned. saturated = slots or a per-minute budget busy (the circuit is not charged); exhausted = window or balance spent (the circuit opens and pins); unknown = unclassified, or rate-limit failover off. A provider at its slot ceiling is a flat line of saturated.

panels.title: Breaker opens/s by cause
panels.description: Breaker open transitions with the verdict phrase that caused them. The state timeline cannot show an open and a close inside one scrape; this can.

panels.title: Failover exhaustion/s by reason
panels.description: Requests a group could not serve at all: no_available_provider (zero candidates), all_busy (the last candidate at capacity), all_failed (anything else, or the deadline). Every point here is a user-visible failure.

panels.title: Quota used
panels.description: Share of each subscription window consumed, from the latest successful quota poll (the same figures the provider's quota modal shows). 100% is spent: the breaker pins the provider until the window rolls over. The bar caps at 100%; the number keeps counting for a balance provider serving into overage. Only providers whose quota endpoint states a measurable window appear.

panels.title: Quota used over time
panels.description: The same windows over the selected range: the slope is the burn rate, a drop is a rollover. A line that reaches 1 and stays there is a window the fleet is routing around until it resets. A dashed yellow line is a provider's quota reserve: routing stops once a window climbs past it. The axis stops at 125%: a provider serving into overage still shows above 100%, and a larger overage reads from the Quota used gauge beside this panel and from the tooltip rather than stretching the scale.

panels.title: Resets in
panels.description: Time until each dated window rolls over. A balance with no reset (prepaid credits) is not listed. Negative means the poll has not run since the rollover.

panels.title: Goroutines
panels.description: Live goroutines in the gateway process. A staircase that never comes back down is a leak.

panels.title: Resident memory
panels.description: Resident set size of the gateway process.

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: Process CPU burn: 100% is one core fully busy.
